title: Not a checklist: an "is everything okay?" glance dashboard whose status rows update live from a store
prompt: Build a glance dashboard that answers "is everything okay?" at a look. It shows three rows: the baby monitor (state ok, "Sleeping since 13:10"), a package (state warn, "En route, arriving today") and the home server (state ok, "Up, 12 days"). Each row has a label, a one-line detail and a state of ok, warn or bad that is visible at a glance (color plus text, not color alone). The values live in a <ui-store name="home"> in the page shell, shaped {"baby": {"state": "ok", "detail": "Sleeping since 13:10"}, "package": {...}, "server": {...}}, and the rows must update live when the store changes (for example when server.state becomes "bad"), with no inline script. This is a monitor, not a to-do list: nothing is checked off. Put the rows inside <main id="outlet">. Use the library's components; do NOT write inline script or onclick handlers.

assert.step: Three status rows in the outlet, and no to-do list dressed up as a dashboard

assert.eval: (() => { const s = [...document.querySelectorAll('#outlet ui-status')].find(x => /baby/i.test(x.label)); return !!s && s.state === 'ok' && s.detail === 'Sleeping since 13:10'; })()

(() => { const f = (re) => [...document.querySelectorAll('#outlet ui-status')].find(x => re.test(x.label)); return f(/package/i)?.state === 'warn' && f(/server/i)?.state === 'ok' && f(/server/i).detail === 'Up, 12 days'; })()

assert.step: The state is written out in text, not shown by color alone
The store reports the server down (a ui-action on the home store)
assert.eval: (() => { for (const [path, value] of [['server.state', 'bad'], ['server.detail', 'Down since 14:02']]) document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('ui-action', {detail: {store: 'home', action: 'set', payload: {path, value}}})); return true; })()

assert.step: The server row turned bad live, says so in text and shows the new detail
assert.eval: (() => { const s = [...document.querySelectorAll('#outlet ui-status')].find(x => /server/i.test(x.label)); return s.state === 'bad' && s.detail === 'Down since 14:02' && /problem/i.test(s.shadowRoot.textContent); })()

assert.step: The other rows did not change
assert.eval: (() => { const f = (re) => [...document.querySelectorAll('#outlet ui-status')].find(x => re.test(x.label)); return f(/baby/i).state === 'ok' && f(/package/i).state === 'warn'; })()
